summaries.summary: Power User is an Oracle Cloud EPM predefined role that sits above User and below Service Administrator, inheriting User access. It matters for automation because EPM Automate runDataRule needs Service Administrator or Power User, and runBusinessRule also needs Launch access to the rule. A future update will require Power Users to have write access, not just read access, to a folder before creating forms, dashboards or subfolders in it.

Oracle's Cloud EPM REST API covers Planning, FCCS, Tax Reporting, Account Reconciliation, Data Integration, migration and identity. URLs follow the base-URL/context/rest/version pattern, and version strings are case sensitive. OAuth 2 (a user-context public client, OCI Gen 2 only) is recommended over Basic auth. Basic-auth users with MFA cannot call it, and from 26.11 usernames prefixed with the account name are rejected. Oracle documents no rate limit or 429 code, so treat 503 as retryable.

Service Administrator is the top Oracle Cloud EPM application role and inherits Power User access. An EPM automation user normally needs it: most EPM Automate commands require it (EPMAT-9 means the role is insufficient), as do running Data Integration Pipelines over REST and downloading compliance reports. Service Administrators assign application and granular roles, manage Access Control groups and set OAuth token expiry, without needing to be domain admins.

Cloud Run is Google Cloud's serverless container platform and a deployment target for ADK agents (adk deploy cloud_run) and custom MCP servers over Streamable HTTP, not stdio. Deploying needs roles/run.developer, iam.serviceAccountUser on the runtime service account and Artifact Registry reader. Services are private by default and callers use Invoker with an ID token or IAP. ADK sessions are in memory unless external services are configured. Requests can run up to 60 minutes.

Codex is OpenAI's coding agent, available in ChatGPT apps, the Codex CLI, the IDE extension and Codex Cloud, with an SDK and GitHub Action. Sign-in uses ChatGPT (plan limits, workspace RBAC) or an API key (API billing, no cloud features). Local use and Codex cloud must be granted as workspace permissions. Automation uses Codex access tokens or service accounts, and workload identity federation is in beta. Docs now live on learn.chatgpt.com.

Codex access tokens are OpenAI personal access tokens for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise workspaces. Each one acts as the member who created it and is used for non-interactive codex exec and app-server automation, with Codex and Workspace Agents scopes. The workspace must allow members to create personal access tokens, and an owner sets the expiration limit. Scoped tokens must expire, with a minimum validity of 1 day. They are read from CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN.

The Codex CLI is OpenAI's open-source (Apache-2.0, Rust) terminal coding agent. The latest release is 0.169.0, installed via npm, a PowerShell script, curl or Homebrew. Sign-in options are codex login (ChatGPT), an API key, device auth (beta) or CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, and service accounts need 0.142.0 or later. Admins can force the login method and workspace. MCP servers are added with codex mcp add over stdio or Streamable HTTP, with OAuth.

Conditional Access for agents is Microsoft Entra's policy control for Agent ID identities. It requires Microsoft 365 E7, or an Agent 365 license with Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3. Targeting depends on access type: the user for on-behalf-of, the agent identity or blueprint for app-only, and Agent Users for agent user accounts. Policies don't apply when an agent authenticates with an API key.

The Conversational Analytics API (geminidataanalytics.googleapis.com) is Google Cloud's API behind BigQuery data agents. It has been GA for BigQuery and Looker since 2026-06-23, with v1 REST endpoints and SDKs in seven languages. BigQuery Graph sources went GA on 2026-09-30. Deep Dive thinking mode and the AlloyDB, Cloud SQL and Spanner sources are in preview.

Copilot Credits are Microsoft's common consumption unit for Copilot Studio agents, agent flows, Copilot Chat agents for unlicensed users, Copilot Cowork and the Work IQ API. They replaced messages in September 2025. Usage-based billing is set up in Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot > Cost Management. Global and Billing Administrators manage billing methods, AI and License Administrators can edit but not create spending policies, and readers are view-only. Prepaid packs are consumed first, then P3, then pay-as-you-go.

The Copilot package catalog API is the Microsoft Graph surface for Agent 365's Agent Registry, at /v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages plus package details. It lets tooling list agents programmatically. Calls need the CopilotPackages.Read.All permission and the AI Administrator role. It is in preview as of 2026-11-14.

The Copilot Retrieval API is Microsoft's RAG endpoint, GA since November 2025. It returns text chunks from the Microsoft 365 Copilot hybrid index across SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot connectors, with KQL filtering. Pro-code custom engine agents use it with Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All, or ExternalItem.Read.All for connectors. Limits are 200 requests per user per hour and 25 results per request. Malformed filters silently run unscoped. Pay-as-you-go access for unlicensed users is in preview and excludes OneDrive.

Copilot Studio is Microsoft's agent builder, organised around Microsoft Copilot, Customer Conversation (preview) and standard harnesses. Makers need a tenant Copilot Credit pack plus a User License or authors-group membership, and the Environment Maker Dataverse role. Since July 2026 every new agent gets an Entra Agent ID. Agents call MCP servers over Streamable HTTP only and can use Anthropic, OpenAI and Mistral models. Agents are blocked at 125% of prepaid capacity unless pay-as-you-go is linked.

Agent flows are Copilot Studio standard-harness workflows from Microsoft, billed in Copilot Credits rather than Power Platform requests, so they avoid the 250,000-request cap for Copilot Studio-triggered cloud flows. Power Automate cloud flows can be converted irreversibly, and the environment needs prepaid credits or pay-as-you-go. Since May 2026, asynchronous responses let long runs exceed the two-minute limit. Agent, prompt and Microsoft 365 Copilot nodes are available.

Computer use, GA since May 2026, lets Microsoft Copilot Studio agents operate Windows web and desktop apps with a virtual mouse and keyboard. It requires generative orchestration and costs 5 Copilot Credits per step on standard models or 15 on premium models, even for Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users. GA models are OpenAI CUA, GPT-6 Sol and Claude Sonnet 4.5, which requires the external-models admin setting. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 are experimental.

The MCP client channel, in preview and limited to early-release environments, publishes a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent as a remote MCP server; an A2A client channel works alongside it. Clients authenticate through an Entra app registration with the delegated MCS.InvokeAsMCP scope against API app ID 6f46e6ed-07bf-4616-80f0-47546850f654. If that API isn't visible in Entra, opening the channel once provisions it. Usage consumes Copilot Credits.

The standard harness is the Microsoft Copilot Studio runtime for classic topics, rule-based agents and agent flows, with GPT-5.5 Chat as the default model. It bills in Copilot Credits only after publish: 1 per classic answer, 2 per generative answer, 5 per agent action or computer-use step, 10 for tenant Graph grounding and 13 per 100 flow actions. Reasoning models add 10 credits per 1,000 tokens.

The Cortex Agent SDK is Snowflake's client library, published as the TypeScript package @snowflake/cortex-agent-sdk with the Python import root cortex_agent_sdk. It wraps inline and object agent runs, the managed coding agent and CoCo sessions, and can attach Snowflake MCP servers. It is in preview and available to all accounts as of 2026-11-14. The Python pip package name is unconfirmed.

Cortex Agents are Snowflake's agent service. They orchestrate Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, custom tools, MCP connectors, web search and code execution, and Snowflake now recommends them over standalone Analyst. Callers need SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER or the narrower CORTEX_AGENT_USER, USAGE on the agent, and their own grants on every tool object; inaccessible tools are skipped by default. Agents are called through REST, with X-Snowflake-Role selecting the role. Billing is by tokens plus each tool's cost. Guardrails have been GA since May 2026.

MCP connectors let Snowflake Cortex Agents call external MCP servers, with prebuilt connectors for Atlassian, GitHub, Glean, Linear and Salesforce. An admin creates an API integration with API_PROVIDER = external_mcp, using OAuth2 client credentials or dynamic client registration, plus an EXTERNAL MCP SERVER object added to the agent spec. Only OAuth and tools are supported. Refresh tokens must last at least 3600 seconds, and disabling the integration invalidates user tokens immediately.

The Cortex Agents REST API is Snowflake's interface for agent object CRUD under /api/v2/databases/{db}/schemas/{schema}/agents and for runs, either on an object or inline via /api/v2/cortex/agent:run. Results stream as SSE events, and clients must tolerate unknown event types. Requests time out after 15 minutes. Background runs need threads, last up to 6 hours and are available on AWS and Azure only. Run events can be streamed only up to 5 minutes after completion.

Cortex AI Functions (AISQL) are Snowflake SQL functions such as AI_COMPLETE, AI_CLASSIFY, AI_EXTRACT, AI_EMBED and AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT, running OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek and xAI models inside Snowflake. They replace the legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX functions and are available on all editions. Calling them needs the USE AI FUNCTIONS privilege plus CORTEX_USER or the scalar-only AI_FUNCTIONS_USER role. Billing is per million tokens. No SQL throughput limit is documented.

Cortex AI Gateway is a single per-account Snowflake gateway object named SNOWFLAKE. It gives coding agents, third-party clients and SDKs one governed inference endpoint with traces, cost attribution, budgets and per-user quotas. Inference, observability and cost management went GA on 2026-11-03, and Tools (MCP) is in preview. Access uses the USAGE and MONITOR privileges. Preview commands snow ai claude and snow ai opencode route local agents through it.

Cortex AI Guardrails is Snowflake's detection of prompt injection, including indirect injection in tool outputs, and jailbreaks. It is GA for Snowflake CoCo, CoWork and Cortex Agents. It requires Enterprise edition or higher and a cross-region inference setting such as ANY_REGION or AWS_US. ACCOUNTADMIN enables it through AI_SETTINGS, and activity is logged in CORTEX_AI_GUARDRAILS_USAGE_HISTORY. Whether it redacts PII is unconfirmed.

Cortex Analyst is Snowflake's GA text-to-SQL service over structured data, defined preferably by semantic views and available on all editions. Callers need CORTEX_USER or CORTEX_ANALYST_USER, plus SELECT on tables, stage access for YAML models and USAGE on any Cortex Search services. Its model is not configurable. It bills per successful message plus warehouse time, on legacy Platform Credits. Snowflake now recommends Cortex Agents instead, which can call it as a tool.

Cortex Guard is Snowflake's output safety filter for AI_COMPLETE and COMPLETE, built on Meta Llama Guard 3. It is GA since July 2024 but off by default, and is enabled with guardrails: TRUE in the model options. It is billed on input tokens on top of the AI_COMPLETE charge.

Cortex Knowledge Extensions are Snowflake Cortex Search services that providers share through Marketplace, private or organizational listings. Consumers use them from AI Functions, Cortex Agents or CoWork to ground agents in third-party content, and a SOURCE_URL column enables citations. Usage-based billing is not supported, and they cannot be used in listings with Egress Cost Optimizer.

Cortex model RBAC is Snowflake's model-level access control. It uses SNOWFLAKE application roles such as CORTEX-MODEL-ROLE-ALL and per-model roles, with model objects in SNOWFLAKE.MODELS refreshed daily. It replaces CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST, which can only be set to 'None' since 2026-08-05 and fully retires in January 2027. Accounts that had 'All' get the ALL role through PUBLIC until it is revoked. ACCOUNTADMIN always keeps model access.

The Cortex REST API is Snowflake's inference API on the account URL under /api/v2/cortex/v1. It offers OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions, Anthropic-compatible /messages for Claude, and /responses (preview since 2026-10-23). The default role needs CORTEX_USER or CORTEX_REST_API_USER. Rate limits are per account per model in RPM and TPM and return 429 when exceeded. max_completion_tokens defaults to 4,096, and requests are capped at 20 MiB.

Cortex Search is Snowflake's managed hybrid vector and keyword search for RAG and agents, available on all editions and usable as a Cortex Agents tool. Creating a service needs CREATE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE, SELECT on sources, a warehouse and CORTEX_USER or CORTEX_EMBED_USER. Querying needs USAGE on the service, database and schema, and searches run with owner's rights. Serving is billed per GB-month even when idle. Limits are 20 QPS per service and 140 QPS per account.

Custom engine agents are Microsoft 365 Copilot agents that bring their own orchestrator and model. They can be built with Copilot Studio, the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, the Teams SDK or Microsoft Foundry, and require app manifest version 1.21 or later. Pro-code versions reach Microsoft 365 data through Microsoft Graph and the Copilot Retrieval API, whereas Copilot Studio agents have native access.

The Customer Conversation harness is a Microsoft Copilot Studio runtime for voice and chat customer service with human escalation. It has been in preview since October 2026 and is still labelled preview. It uses a different usage-based billing model from the standard harness.

Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) on Google Cloud's Agent Platform cover Agent Runtime, sandboxes, endpoints, models, datasets, batch jobs, pipelines and Vector Search. CMEK for Gemini 3 tuning went GA on 2026-10-19. The Agent Platform Service Agent needs roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key. The key must be in the resource's region, except that Gemini Live and Interactions API serving profiles need us or eu keys.

Data 360, formerly Data Cloud, is Salesforce's data platform that grounds Agentforce through Agent Context Engine, Persistent Agent Memory and Trusted Grounding. It offers zero-copy links to Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and AWS. A Data 360 admin assigns its permission sets, such as Data Cloud User. Agent observability relies on Session Trace Data Model records, which need the Agentforce Activity data stream. Pricing uses Flex Credits ($500 per 100k) or profiles, and the hosted MCP server needs API v66.0+.

Databricks, whose platform is now called the Data + AI Platform, offers Agent Bricks for building agents, plus Omnigent. It bills in DBUs per second. Engineers need a workspace user, a service principal with OAuth or workload identity federation, Unity Catalog grants and warehouse and serving permissions. Private connectivity uses PrivateLink, Private Link or Private Service Connect depending on the cloud. Recent renames include Vector Search to AI Search and Genie Spaces to Genie Agents. No A2A support was found.

Account admin is the top Databricks administrative role, above workspace, metastore, Marketplace and billing admins. Account admins create workspaces, add service principals and assign them to workspaces, and enable RBAC for the account. They also manage the access denylist, context-based ingress rules and network connectivity configurations for serverless private endpoints. Enabling the Enhanced Unity Gateway preview, needed for the Beta system.ai MCP servers, also requires an account admin.

Databricks account-level SSO provides unified login through SAML 2.0 or OIDC. It is mandatory for accounts created after 2023-06-21 or without SSO configured before 2024-12-12. Once enabled, all users including admins sign in via SSO, except up to 20 emergency access users who use a password and security key.

Agent Runtime is the Databricks Agent Bricks component that hosts an agent server at an authenticated endpoint and runs on Databricks Apps. For new code agents, Databricks recommends building with the Agent Bricks CLI and DurableAgentServer on Agent Runtime, invoked at /api/invocations.

AI Gateway is the former name of Databricks' Unity Gateway. It was also called Mosaic AI Gateway, and became Unity AI Gateway around April 2026 when it moved into Unity Catalog. Older docs say legacy guardrails on serving endpoints used Llama Guard and Presidio, with up to 20 QPM or TPM rate limits per endpoint, and that output guardrails didn't support embeddings or streaming. Those details are unverified against current Unity Gateway docs.

AI Search is Databricks' vector and full-text retrieval service for agents, renamed from Vector Search on 2026-06-01, though REST paths still use /api/2.0/vector-search. Index types are Delta Sync with managed or self-managed embeddings, Direct Vector Access and a Beta BM25 full-text index. Standard endpoints hold about 320M vectors with high QPS, while storage-optimized endpoints hold over 1B but add latency. Default limits include 50 indexes per endpoint and 200 hybrid results.
